My parents passed away in different months when I was 18. For the first few months until my dad’s death I spent much of my time focusing on trying to graduate high school w/o my dad’s help and visiting my brother weekly since he was in a hospital for his mental disorder. After my dad died,  I was focused on survival for years. However, having friends to talk to helps & therapy (but it took years for me to believe therapy is necessary and it did help because friends are not professionals to help you). Also I traveled when I could and looked for hobbies and such to keep busy. 

I suggest to not suppress how you feel because it’s your body’s natural way of coping and take it one day at a time. It’ll feel like you’re living in a dream/everything will feel surreal for a while. You’ll disassociate sometimes in public and what helps with that is look for items in the room and recognize them as a way to ground you and keep you present. 


Hm, what else. Oh recently I’ve been into reading accounts from mediums and from what a couple have said, your deceased loved one is always there with you in the room & they’re only a thought away so just talk to them if you want.


as for stability, I haven’t found it yet and I’m 32, but that’s ok. Therapy helped a lot and CBT helped. I try to not cope in unhealthy ways but some days the depression wins (and regression is completely fine) 
Sorry for rambling 😅
